control.label: route-b27-head-control-1
limitations: Uniform shipment demand is an asymptotic calculation if the observed MTP pattern repeats, not an achieved sustained rate. Startup stock, ring prefetch and file-boundary rounding are excluded.
All-group shipments follow the fastest-consumed group. Slower groups may retain unused cells for later use; these are not claimed to be immediately discarded.
Raw USB 5 Gb/s gives a deliberately generous 625 MB/s ceiling before protocol overhead and competing traffic. Both replies and pads travel toward the phone across this physical link.
Smaller shipments reduce the publication unit but retain all groups and do not remove the underlying per-token traffic requirement.
No sparse shipment format or partial-file publication has been implemented.

The source gap surrounds pad acquisition and other work before the next wire call; the independent cumulative pad-wait counter accounts for all but 1.462 ms of it.
Index inference requires the observed initial ledger window starting at zero and unique output-projection frame geometry. Ring cursor advances may precede consumption.
The shipment is currently published only after complete receipt, fsync and judgment. No partial publication was enabled.

b27-guest-sched-1.label: route-b27-guest-sched-1
b27-guest-sched-1.scope: Owned Android bridge, pad stream/fetch, and vhost threads only; other app and vCPU threads excluded.
limitations: Frequency transition events report policy frequency, not retired cycles or proof of thermal throttling.
Weighted only while the identified host thread is scheduled Running; guest execution cannot be assigned to an internal guest thread from host vCPU identity.
Initial time before the first frequency event is unknown and remains excluded from the mean.
Observed app marker windows are clipped to the trace and have the boundary limits documented by scheduler-analysis.json.
